name: Dagger LLM primitive - greetings-api reference
description:
Dagger's built-in LLM primitive (dag.LLM) is the execution model dagmar wants; it is used end-to-end by github.com/kpenfound/greetings-api (see .dagger/develop.go, .dagger/debugger.go, .dagger/review.go).

Core pattern (Go SDK; greetings-api engine v0.20.6, dagmar targets v0.21.8):
  ws := dag.CodeWorkspace(sourceDir, checkable)            // source + a thing that runs build/test/lint
  env := dag.Env().
      WithCodeWorkspaceInput("workspace", ws, "desc").     // code the agent can read/write/test
      WithCodeWorkspaceOutput("completed", "desc")          // declared output workspace
  prompt := dag.CurrentModule().Source().File("prompts/x.md")
  agent := dag.LLM(dagger.LLMOpts{Model: model}).
      WithEnv(env).
      WithPromptFile(prompt).
      Loop()

Extract results:
  agent.Env().Output("completed").AsCodeWorkspace().Work() -> *dagger.Directory
  agent.Env().Output("fixed").AsCodeWorkspace().Diff(ctx)  -> unified diff string
  agent.TokenUsage().TotalTokens(ctx)                       -> cost observability
One-shot (no loop): dag.LLM(opts).WithPrompt("...").LastReply(ctx)

Why it matters for dagmar:
- The agent runs INSIDE the hermetic Dagger engine and self-verifies via the CodeWorkspace checkable (build/test/lint). This is exactly the sandboxed LLM execution + quality gate that Hybrid-C calls for: agent pods invoke the in-cluster engine, which runs dag.LLM().Loop() on a per-task CodeWorkspace of the target repo.
- greetings-api ships a coder->review pipeline (DevelopPullRequest auto-triggers PullRequestReview) and a feedback loop (PullRequestFeedback via slash command) - working precedents for the review-agent QA and the iterative PR flow dagmar wants.
- Prompts are .md files bundled in the module; dagmar will source prompts via canopy (adapter) instead.

Correction to Daggerverse survey (#6): a reusable GitHub PR/issues module DOES exist - github.com/kpenfound/dag/github-issue (Read, CreatePullRequest, CreatePullRequestCommit, WritePullRequestCodeComment, GetPrForCommit). greetings-api depends on it. Default model used there: claude-sonnet-4-0.

name: Future: human-facing Plan-Agent interface (Telegram)
description: Future direction: expose dagmar to humans via a chat interface (Telegram messenger) that accepts prompts and invokes a Plan-Agent, which decomposes work into seeds issues. OUT OF SCOPE FOR NOW: planning is done locally with Wayfinder, translated into seeds issues, then agents work the issues. Consequently 'Plan' is NOT a dagmar Tier-C type today (stays a seeds/IssueTracker concept); revisit when this human-facing Plan-Agent interface is built.

name: Dagger LLM primitive - daggerverse-qa reference
description: Reference for the Dagger LLM primitive applied to NON-INTERACTIVE BATCH AGENTS (complements greetings-api mx-e05f90, which shows Loop() end-to-end on a CodeWorkspace). Source: github.com/levlaz/agent-playground/tree/main/daggerverse-qa -- an automated QA tool that crawls Daggerverse modules, runs QA on each, and emits per-module HTML reports plus an aggregated index, all driven by LLM agents. Pattern: dag.LLM().WithEnv(env).WithPromptFile(dag.CurrentModule().Source().File('qa.prompt')).Env().AsWorkspace().Container(). Build a dag.Workspace, expose it via dag.Env().WithWorkspaceInput('before', ws, 'tools to complete the assignment').WithWorkspaceOutput('after', 'the completed assignment'), drive the agent with a prompt FILE, then materialize output via .AsWorkspace().Container(). Two distinct agents, each with its own .prompt file: Run (per-module QA -> HTML report, qa.prompt) and BuildIndex (aggregate reports -> index.html, index.prompt). Takeaways for dagmar: prompt files are first-class and canopy-composable, and the input/output Workspace env pair is the clean boundary between task input and agent-produced output.

name: k3s Daggerverse module — correct ref
description: Daggerverse k3s module is at github.com/marcosnils/daggerverse/k3s (a subdir of the marcosnils/daggerverse monorepo), NOT github.com/marcosnils/k3s which 404s. The earlier wayfinder note was wrong. Pinned in dagmar dagger.json: source github.com/marcosnils/daggerverse/k3s@k3s/v0.11.1, pin c07646d. Go SDK, engineVersion v0.19.9 (runs fine on engine v0.21.8). API: dag.K3S(name); Server() *Service; Config(K3SConfigOpts{Local bool}) *File (kubeconfig); Kubectl(args string) *Container; Kns().
